- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for high-sentiment or high-activity periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct; apply a “cool-down” penalty: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — forecasts drift toward historical mean; adjust by adding a 1–3% upward bias to counteract downward drift.
- Model underestimates true volatility in late horizon (days 25–30), especially when true outcomes show sharp declines or corrections; increase forecast variance by 0.5–1.0% for final 5–7 days.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% for 2+ consecutive days, model is likely underestimating supply/demand shock — increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment indicates market exhaustion.
- Sentiment history is uniformly zero — no behavioral signal — so model should not assume sentiment-driven momentum; treat as pure technical/price-based model with no behavioral adjustment.
